English: The impact of cyber harm
What is it?

Cyber-crime is often treated as “just money” or “just online”. For victims it can feel like a burglary of the mind: someone they trusted turned out to be a criminal, private images may be seen by others, and family savings may be gone. Many victims blame themselves and hide what happened. Secondary victimisation is harm caused by the reaction of others — family, police, bank staff or helpers — through blame, disbelief or insensitive questions. A First Responder's first job is to make sure it does not happen at their desk.

Psychological first aid: look, listen, link
What is it?

Psychological first aid (PFA) is humane, supportive and practical help for people in distress. It is not counselling or therapy, and it never forces people to talk about what happened. Its three action principles are Look (for safety, urgent needs and severe reactions), Listen (to needs and concerns, and help people feel calm) and Link (to practical help, information, loved ones and services).

Distress, self-harm and safeguarding
What is it?

Sextortion, large financial loss and online abuse can push people into crisis. A First Responder must notice the warning signs and act at once. Safety overrides every other part of the case — evidence, forms and reports can wait.

Child safeguarding

If a child may be at risk of sexual abuse or exploitation — including online grooming or a planned meeting with an adult — inform the police or Special Juvenile Police Unit and Childline 1098 at once. Reporting is a legal duty under POCSO s.19. Do not question the child repeatedly; let trained officers do that. Involve a parent or guardian unless they may be the source of harm.

Checking understanding

Instead of “Do you understand?”, ask the person to say back the next step: “Just so I know I explained it well, what will you do when you get home?” This is called teach-back, and it is the same method used in V1 assessments.

Tech-enabled abuse: a careful approach

When a partner or family member monitors or controls someone through their phone (stalkerware, location sharing, account access), removing it suddenly may alert the abuser and increase danger. First talk about safety, use a safe device for help-seeking, and refer to police, 181 or a One Stop Centre for a safety plan before changing settings.
Confidentiality, closure and self-care
What is it?

A citizen's story, identity and evidence belong to them. Share only what an agency needs, only with consent (except where the law requires reporting, such as child sexual abuse), and never on social media or group chats. A case is closed well when the person knows what happens next and how to reach help.
